nodes.label: Archived Build Plan
nodes.rationale: The authoritative build order for Stages 0-14, superseded in part on 2026-08-09. Reference documents are the authoritative source of what to build; this file is the order to build it in.

nodes.label: Six Prime Directives
nodes.rationale: 1 logic only, no styling (retired at Stage 17). 2 do not invent features. 3 security rules are not negotiable — where any document conflicts with the security specification on a security matter, it wins. 4 stop and ask rather than guess: implement the documented assumption, add TODO(open-question), record it. 5 one stage at a time. 6 tests are part of the stage.

nodes.label: Eighteen Business Rules
nodes.rationale: R1-R18, each mapped to the stage that enforces it. These are the logic; everything else is plumbing. All eighteen have at least one test by Stage 13.

nodes.label: R3 — Sequential Public Numbers, Opaque Internal Reference
nodes.rationale: Membership numbers are sequential and public (PG-0003) while the internal member reference is an opaque random ID. Because the public number is sequential and printed on cards, anything derived from it is guessable — which is why claim codes and identity payloads both use the opaque id instead.

nodes.label: R7 — Redemptions Are Immutable
nodes.rationale: No UPDATE, no DELETE — a correction is a new reversing row. Enforced at the database level rather than in application code, so neither a bug in a handler nor a compromised API process can talk it out of the guarantee.

nodes.label: R10 — The Payload Identifies, Never Authorises
nodes.rationale: Resolving an identity payload returns who the member is and what they are entitled to, and performs no state change. This is the whole basis on which a static printed code later became acceptable: possession of the payload alone is worth nothing.

nodes.label: R11 — No Member Enumeration for Outlet Staff
nodes.rationale: Not filtered — absent. There is no list, search or enumeration endpoint available to the role at all, and the client contains no such call in its API module, so the button does not exist to be found. Adding a member search endpoint for staff convenience is explicitly named as a trap.

nodes.label: R13 — Cohorts Below Five Are Suppressed
nodes.rationale: With a membership of dozens, a report filtered to one benefit, one outlet and one week may describe exactly one person. Without suppression, aggregate reporting becomes an indirect route to individual member movements.

nodes.label: R14 — Benefit Values Are Database Rows
nodes.rationale: The acceptance test for the whole project: changing the dining discount from 25% to 20% must be a database update through an admin endpoint. If it requires a code change the build has failed regardless of what else works. Enforced negatively by a test that scans src/ for printed-sheet values and for a benefit key sitting next to a percentage.

nodes.label: R16 — Members Are Suspended, Never Deleted
nodes.rationale: DELETE on Member is revoked from the application role. This is also what makes deletion-by-anonymisation the only available shape for a deletion request, since severing the link to redemption history lets aggregate reporting survive.

nodes.label: R17 — Every Route Declares a Permission
nodes.rationale: An undeclared route fails at startup — the single most important control in the build. The realistic failure is not a broken check but a new endpoint shipped under deadline with no check at all, so forgetting to protect an endpoint becomes a build failure rather than a hole discovered in production.

nodes.label: R18 — Out-of-Scope Records Return 404
nodes.rationale: A 403 confirms the record exists. An out-of-scope record must be byte-identical to a nonexistent one.

nodes.label: Decided Stack
nodes.rationale: TypeScript strict on Node 20+, Fastify, PostgreSQL 15+, Prisma, Zod, @node-rs/argon2, jose, Vitest + Supertest, React + Vite clients, npm workspaces. Separate React apps rather than one, because they have entirely different authentication and authorization models.

nodes.label: Monorepo Repository Structure
nodes.rationale: docs/ read-only references, apps/api plus one app per client surface, packages/shared for Zod schemas and types, and PROGRESS.md and DECISIONS.md maintained per stage. The root workspaces globs already cover apps/*, so client apps needed no configuration change when they arrived.

nodes.label: Things That Will Go Wrong
nodes.rationale: Money as a float, fetch-then-check authorization, 403 for out-of-scope records, hardcoding benefit percentages to move faster, reading alg from the JWT header, adding a staff member search, making redemptions updatable because reversal seemed complicated, logging a member object, and building a points system that does not exist.

nodes.label: Primary Acceptance Journey
nodes.rationale: Twelve steps in order against one running server, no step stubbed, each using what the previous produced — from administrator creating a member through to the headline pair: changing the dining discount to 20% and the member client reflecting it with no restart or deployment.
